changes.evidence: The initial is a long vertical stroke with a hooked lower end, rising approximately to the height of the following l strokes. No separate dot is visible. That supports capital J, but the form is also compatible with an undotted lower-case j; the crop does not settle case.
The four digits stand below the month at the right edge, visibly on a second baseline. The place and day/month occupy the upper baseline.
A long descending p is followed by a small closed a body and the short shoulder/exit of r. The three letters are legible in the half.

The low horizontal stroke under the left part of the word curves directly into the descending stroke of g. It is one continuous g descender, not an independent underline; no separate emphasis stroke appears under the rest of the word.

changes.h: es-tu; note describes es written over est
changes.evidence: After the readable e and s, several short heavy transverse cancellation strokes cover a tall stem and a small looped foot. A former t is plausible, but the crossing prevents a certain letter identification. The cancellation itself is certain.

After ser ai, the terminal rises into a tall loop and comes down into a heavily retraced low loop with a rightward finish. The tall form supports t, while the doubled curve remains compatible with s. Neither candidate is eliminated by the crop.

changes.location: Paragraph 2, physical line break between serait/serais and tu
changes.final: serait/serais tu, with no supplied joining hyphen
changes.evidence: The right-hand word ends in its looped terminal with blank paper after it; the next line begins directly with tu. There is no dash at the end of the first line or before tu. The crop covers only the first side; the beginning of the next line was settled in half a.

There are two detached dark marks, one above the other. The upper is nearly round; the lower is heavier with a small hook. Their separation resembles a colon, but a highly compressed accented à cannot be excluded from these strokes.

The crop gives a clear tall descending f, a low connected group, a prominent narrow loop/ascender in the middle-right, a detached high i-like stroke, and an angular final s. The compact word favours favoris, but I cannot assign all the middle strokes securely or exclude the alternative fantaisies. The lexical disagreement is therefore retained as an explicit uncertainty.
The initial n and a sit on the baseline; the g has a descending loop with a leftward tail, followed by a low e and short r exit. The full sequence is readable in half b.

The line below lon is joined continuously to the descending right side of g and turns back left. There is no independent underline: the observed stroke is the g tail, matching the separate inspection of cogitations.
The first e has a short high accent stroke. Above i is a single compact dot, with no paired legs or roof-shaped circumflex. The crop settles the spelling without a circumflex.

Repeated oblique cancellation strokes intersect a low series of loops and one surviving tall medial stem. Individual letters and word division remain insecure. The surviving connected run is kept as one estimated unreadable word; two short words are possible, but I cannot establish a division from the ink.

changes.location: Paragraph 3, word between une and approche
changes.evidence: After the p-r-e-m group and dotted i, a small e body has a near-vertical grave-like stroke above it; the word ends in the rightward r shoulder. Blank space separates that r from approche, and no final e loop or exit is present.

A long cancellation line crosses the word. A small initial vowel/angled group, a tall medial loop compatible with d, and a run of lower humps ending in a raised final stroke support évidemment, but the overwriting prevents certainty for the entire sequence. The reading remains marked, and the crossed state is clear.

A small detached descending hook sits below and immediately right of the cancelled word, before the large loop beginning le. It is not crossed by the cancellation line. This is a live comma retained after the substituted bien sûr.

The first low horizontal traces are partly washed out. A distinct low vertical tail at the left favours q, and a detached high mark at the right can be an apostrophe. Several nearby surface dots weaken the assignment of the high mark, and the incomplete letter bodies leave où au possible. The following au is visible.

notes: This is the first page of cote 134-2, so the reading begins with \cotefile{134-2}. The author page number is 1; the archive foliation is 146. The heading gives Villecun, 17/19 Juillet/juillet, and 1975 on a separate line.

The opening congratulates Larry on the birth of his daughter. The next paragraph asks about nationality and academic status in France, a possible position at Montpellier, and visits to Montpellier or Villecun.

Author qualifications are preserved: Si cela pouvait s'arranger; pour le moment; guère; and seulement partiellement. These describe conditional plans and the author's limited ability to follow the work, not established mathematical conclusions.

The author describes a proposed non-strict n-category construction and a nerve functor. He calls it a first precise approach, while qualifying its merit with certes and bien sûr, and criticizes it as très technique and peu intuitive. The type of theory is one que je prévois. These are the author's assessments, not reader verification.
The n in n-catégorie and the numeral 1 in 1-cat. prompted explicit glyph inspection in the halves. The page stops after 1-cat. et. No completion from another page is supplied.

No independent mathematical argument, derivation, proof check or background-theorem check was performed. The checks array is therefore empty; ordinary transcription is not reported as mathematical verification.

The two H emphasis marks were inspected separately. Both low rules are continuous left-sweeping g descenders; no separate underline was established. The marks around the final connective include surface dots, and no additional intentional punctuation omitted by both witnesses could be established.

The started_utc value is the first explicitly captured UTC time in this independent pass, after the initial packet and three prescribed image views; it is not an invented timestamp for the earlier un-timed start.

coverage: I viewed the whole 1688 × 2372 source once for layout, then each supplied 1688 × 1266 half once in sequence. Every heading word, body line, agreed C/H word, ending, accent, punctuation mark, correction and page number was read against the ink. The letter contains three body paragraphs, two additions, three cancellations (including the letter in es-tu), no mathematical display, diagram or drawing, and no independent margin note. The lower paragraph continues off the sheet and is left incomplete after et. Eleven tight crops address only unresolved loci; adjacent issues share the relevant crop without redundant re-cropping. H's one-line heading placement, uncertainties, two emphasis marks, added hyphen, lexical reading, spelling choices, unreadable cancellation and omitted comma are accounted for. No independent block of text missing from both witnesses was found. All unresolved readings remain marked in reading.tex; both sides of the questioned line break and the insertion spanning two lines have source-pixel boxes.
